A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exercise‑induced recovery is not a general phenomenon but rather depends on a specific exercise regimen and on the lesion site.
the effects of exercise on cognitive performance after brain damage are highly dependent on the exercise protocol used and the type of brain injury.
FF transection induced a long‑lasting impairment in place learning, which could not be reversed by any of the exercise regimens tested.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exercise‑induced recovery potential of a given exercise protocol needs to be tested for each brain lesion location and cognitive task separately.
exercise can be beneficial for the recovery of cognitive performance only when it is administered before or immediately after the lesion.
the exercise regimen should be tailored to the type of brain injury and the cognitive task.
